items_in_category: I can be silent next to you
I don't gossip about loved ones
I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Поддерживаю без советов, умею молчать рядом, помогаю без ожидания, слушаю по-настоящему. Твой green flag — присутствие, не действие.
current_p1_en:
You support without advice, can sit quietly next to someone, help without expectation, and really listen. Your green flag is presence, not performance.
You understand that helping doesn't always mean solving the problem. Sometimes it means being there.
People love you for it. When they feel bad, they come to you — because you won't immediately advise.
What's worth knowing: quiet support sometimes reads as "you have no opinion". Learn to feel. When the other really needs advice — give it. When they need to just be heard — be silent. Different skills, both valuable.

items_in_category: I can be silent next to you
I don't gossip about loved ones
I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Говорю правду, могу сказать «я был неправ», не ищу виноватых, извиняюсь первым. Твой green flag — целостность даже в мелочах. Где другие выкручиваются, ты говоришь как есть.
current_p1_en:
You tell the truth, can say "I was wrong," don't look for someone to blame, and apologize first. Your green flag is integrity even in small things. Where others wriggle out, you say it plainly.
You have your own dignity. A liar constantly tracks what they told whom; you don't.
People sometimes ask: "you really said it like that?" Like that. Living with yourself matters more than living with their approval.
What's worth knowing: "always the truth" sometimes becomes a relationship test. If you're not loved for honesty, that's not about you — that's about their unreadiness for it. Accept it. And not all truths must be said immediately — timing is also wisdom.

items_in_category: I can be silent next to you
I don't gossip about loved ones
I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Радуюсь успехам друзей искренне, поддерживаю без советов, помогаю без ожидания, не осуждаю. Твой green flag — отсутствие зависти.
current_p1_en:
You're sincerely happy for friends' wins, support without advice, help without expectation, and don't judge. Your green flag is the absence of envy.
You have your own self-sufficiency. Someone else's success doesn't threaten you; you're grounded in your own truth.
People sometimes don't believe it: "you don't envy?" You don't. Their success is theirs. Yours is ahead, or already happened.
What's worth knowing: being glad for others is also a skill. If it comes automatically, wonderful. If you have to strain, it's worth understanding why. Envy is a normal feeling; working with it is adult practice.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: План и расписание, помидоро 25/5, список задач как фетиш, утро — святое. Ты работаешь по системе, и эта система — твоя свобода.
current_p1_en:
Plans, schedules, Pomodoro 25/5, to-do lists as a ritual, sacred mornings. You work through a system — and that system is your freedom.
You know that without structure, you'd drown in chaos. Most people fear a strict schedule; you found the freedom inside it. Fewer decisions, more motion.
People sometimes call you a "nerd". Maybe. But you get three times as much done.
What's worth knowing: rigid systems are useful, but they break under the unexpected. Add buffer. A day planned at 100% becomes stress at the first call from your mom. A day planned at 70% is realistic.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: Утро — святое, план и расписание, тихий фокус, делаю сам. Ты работаешь до 12:00 — в эти часы ты непобедим(-а). Дальше — вторичные задачи.
current_p1_en:
Morning is sacred: plan, schedule, quiet focus, do it yourself. You work until noon, and in those hours you're almost unbeatable. After that, secondary tasks can take over.
Your circadian rhythm is built this way. Most people try to be productive all day; you know you have a window, and you use it fully.
People are sometimes surprised: "you're working at 8 AM?" Yes. And by noon you're in a café or at the gym. Not for everyone.
What's worth knowing: morning mode works only if you sleep early. If you try to be both lark and owl, burnout arrives in months.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: Ночной рывок, тихий фокус, интуитивно без системы, дедлайн. Ты включаешься после 23:00. Когда мир спит, у тебя начинается своя жизнь.
current_p1_en:
Night sprint, quiet focus, intuition over system, deadline pressure. You switch on after 11 PM. When the world sleeps, your life starts.
Your biology is set differently. The office-day noise dulls you; night silence wakes you up.
People worry: "you don't sleep." You do. Just at a different time.
What's worth knowing: night mode clashes with a world that runs by day. If your work demands daytime hours, you're chronically sleep-deprived. Ask yourself whether you can move real work to the night without breaking your body.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: Тихий фокус с наушниками, делаю сам, помидоро, утро. Тебе нужна тишина и одиночество. Никакого open space, никакого шума, никаких людей рядом во время работы.
current_p1_en:
Quiet focus with headphones, solo work, Pomodoro, morning hours. You need silence and solitude. No open space, no background noise, no people hovering beside you while you work.
You have deep concentration, but small interruptions knock you off track. So you build an environment with fewer small interruptions.
People sometimes don't get it: "you don't socialize at the office?" You do — just not while working. Different modes.
What's worth knowing: silence mode works only if you can protect the environment. If you work in a noisy open space, buy serious noise-canceling headphones. Don't cheap out — that's your productivity tool.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: В команде и общей энергии, в кафе с людьми, несколько потоков сразу, интуитивно. Тебе нужны люди рядом, чтобы работать. В одиночку — скучно и медленно.
current_p1_en:
Team energy, cafés with people, several streams at once, intuitive rhythm. You need people around to work. Alone, everything gets boring and slow.
You're a social animal. Other people's rhythm lifts you. When someone nearby is doing the work, you start doing yours too.
People are sometimes surprised: "you work in a noisy café?" Yes. More efficiently than at home.
What's worth knowing: social style needs places with the right atmosphere. Not every coworking fits. Find your places — the ones where work flows — and don't ditch them for short-term savings.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: Много маленьких задач, список с галочками, помидоро, план. Тебе нужна структура из микро-целей. Большая задача тебя пугает; разбитая на 20 маленьких — заходит легко.
current_p1_en:
Many small tasks, checkboxes, Pomodoro, a plan. You need a structure of micro-goals. One big task scares you; broken into 20 small ones, it becomes manageable.
You get dopamine from finishing. Each checkmark is a small win, and the day is built from those wins.
People sometimes say: "you could've done one big thing." Maybe. But ten small completed things feel better to you than one big thing still unfinished.
What's worth knowing: small wins can keep you away from the important work. Small tasks are often urgent, not important. Learn to balance. Sometimes you need to take on one big thing and give up the daily satisfaction.

items_in_category: In a team and shared energy
current_p1_ru: Только в идеальных условиях, только что нравится, утро, тихий фокус. Тебе нужны правильные условия, чтобы работать. Без них — не пишется, не делается, не идёт.
current_p1_en:
Ideal conditions, work you actually care about, morning, quiet focus. You need the right environment before work starts to flow.
You're highly sensitive to surroundings. Some people can work in any basement; you need specific light, sound, coffee, weather. So you build the conditions.
People call this "fussy". Not fussy — a system.
What's worth knowing: ideal conditions rarely arrive on their own. If you wait for them, you do nothing. Learn to work in imperfect conditions too, or you become hostage to the environment. And remember: "I like this" is not always the main criterion. Sometimes you have to do work you don't love, and that is part of growing.

current_p1_ru: Ради еды в любую страну, local experience, пляжный лежебока, люксовый турист. Тебе нужно есть. Каждое путешествие — это в первую очередь карта ресторанов и местных рынков.
current_p1_en:
You'll fly to any country for the food. Local markets, beach lunches, luxury restaurants — every trip begins as a map of where to eat.
You have a strong sense of taste. You don't travel to tick off the Eiffel Tower; you want to feel a country through its flavors.
People sometimes don't get it: "you went for the food?" For the food. What's wrong with that? Food is culture.
What's worth knowing: gastro-tourism gets expensive. Good restaurants, Michelin stars, private tours — it adds up. Learn to balance the budget. And remember: street food is often tastier and more honest than starred places.

current_p1_ru: Музеи, галереи, фотограф, медленный путешественник. Тебе нужна культура. Не «расслабиться» — а узнать, погрузиться, увидеть.
current_p1_en:
Museums, galleries, slow walks, photos for one exact angle. You need culture. Not just "rest", but learning, immersion, seeing.
Travel is education for you, not escape. You want to come back with more than a tan.
People get tired: "three museums today already?" Three. And another tomorrow.
What's worth knowing: cultural tourism takes stamina. Hours of museum walking wear you out. Plan pauses. And don't try to cover everything — better one museum deeply than ten at surface level.

current_p1_ru: Шезлонг с книгой, люкс, шоппинг, медленный путешественник. Тебе нужен отдых. Не приключения; не культура. Лежать, читать, ничего не делать.
current_p1_en:
A lounger with a book, a nice hotel, shopping, slow travel. You need rest. Not adventure, not culture. Lying down, reading, doing nothing.
Your life is intense enough already. Travel is a pause, not a suitcase stuffed with achievements.
People accuse you: "you were in Paris and only saw the hotel?" Yes. You were tired and needed the pool.
What's worth knowing: beach rest works when it's conscious. If you "didn't make it to anything interesting", that's on you. You can combine: lie down in the morning, walk in the evening. That's not laziness; it's different tempo at different times.

current_p1_ru: Горы, трекинг, дайвинг, бэкпекер, путешествуешь один, фотограф. Тебе нужно приключение. Не «отдых»; не «культура». Адреналин, сложность, испытание.
current_p1_en:
Mountains, trekking, diving, backpacking, solo travel, chasing one impossible shot. You need adventure. Not "rest", not "culture" — adrenaline, difficulty, a test.
Your nervous system wants intensity. Most people use vacation to find peace; you use it to cut through routine grayness.
People worry: "Nepal alone?" Alone. And it was the best thing you did.
What's worth knowing: extreme travel carries real risk. Don't neglect insurance, guides, or local rules. The most experienced travelers die in mountains they thought they knew.

current_p1_ru: Спонтанные билеты, плановик, люкс, шоппинг. У тебя одна из крайностей: либо «купил билет — завтра летишь», либо «расписан каждый час маршрута».
current_p1_en:
Spontaneous tickets, strict itineraries, luxury bookings, shopping routes. You're at one extreme: either "bought the ticket, flying tomorrow" or "every hour is scheduled."
You have a clear style. Most people sit in the middle — plan a little, improvise a little, and end up in chronic chaos. You commit.
People don't always get it: "how can you go without a plan?" Or: "how can you live by such a rigid schedule?" Depends which version of you they meet.
What's worth knowing: both styles have weak points. Spontaneous travelers often overpay; planners sometimes miss the best thing because it wasn't on the plan. Learn at least a little from the other camp.

current_p1_ru: Только мегаполисы, шоппинг, фотограф, музеи. Тебе скучна природа. Нужны кварталы, культура, движение.
current_p1_en:
Big cities, shopping, photography, museums. Nature bores you. You need neighborhoods, culture, motion.
You have a passion for human life. Nature is for rest; the city is for impressions.
People don't always share it: "you don't love mountains?" No. The city is closer.
What's worth knowing: urban tourism exhausts. Noise, crowds, packed streets. If you only do cities, you come back more tired than when you left. At least once a year, drag yourself into nature for a reset.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Мастер и Маргарита, Преступление и наказание, Война и мир, Лолита. Ты в русской традиции. Не школьная программа; а живое чтение, в котором эти книги до сих пор актуальны.
current_p1_en:
The Master and Margarita, Crime and Punishment, War and Peace, Lolita. You're in the Russian tradition. Not as a school assignment — as living reading, where these books still feel current.
It works because you have a deep relationship with language. Russian prose has its own density, and you feel it.
Other people sometimes stare: "Dostoevsky for fun?" For fun. What's wrong with that?
What's worth knowing: Russian classics need context. Without understanding the era, much is lost. Learn history in parallel. And don't rush — better to read one 600-page book slowly than three quickly.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: 1984, 451 градус, Сияние, Мастер и Маргарита. Тебя цепляют книги, которые предупреждают. Не «развлекательное чтение»; а серьёзное размышление о мире и человеке.
current_p1_en:
1984, Fahrenheit 451, The Shining, The Master and Margarita. What grabs you are books that warn. Not entertainment reading, but serious reflection on the world and the human.
Why this lands: you have civic instincts. Most people read for pleasure; you — to understand where society is heading.
Other people sometimes say: "you're gloomy". Not gloomy — attentive. These books aren't written by accident.
What's worth knowing: dystopias hit hard. Read several in a row and you start feeling "it's all over". Learn to alternate with more positive literature. Reality is more complex, and books are part of the picture, not the whole.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Гарри Поттер, Властелин колец, Игра престолов, Дюна. Тебе нужны большие миры. Не «одна книга»; а серия, в которой ты живёшь годами.
current_p1_en:
Harry Potter, The Lord of the Rings, A Game of Thrones, Dune. You need big worlds. Not one book, but a series you can live inside for years.
The logic is simple: you have patience and love for worlds. Many books feel cramped; you need something to live inside.
Other people sometimes don't get it: "how many times have you reread Harry Potter?". As many as needed. It's home.
What's worth knowing: series often sag. Five Martin books — three brilliant, two weak. Check fan ratings before each next one. And don't be afraid to drop a series that lost quality.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Сто лет одиночества, Мастер и Маргарита, Маленький принц, Лолита. Тебе нравятся книги, в которых реальность размыта. Не «фэнтези» в чистом виде; а проза, в которой сны и явь сплетаются.
current_p1_en:
One Hundred Years of Solitude, The Master and Margarita, The Little Prince, Lolita. You like books where reality blurs. Not pure fantasy, but prose where dream and daily life are woven together.
This works because you have a poetic perception. Pure realism bores you; you need something with a different texture.
Other people sometimes don't share it: "One Hundred Years of Solitude is just nonsense." The so-called nonsense is exactly Márquez's genius. Literature can be illogical and only grow stronger for it.
What's worth knowing: magical realism needs attention. If you read Márquez on the subway between notifications, you lose half. Carve out quiet time.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Великий Гэтсби, Убить пересмешника, Над пропастью во ржи, Сияние. Ты любишь американскую литературу XX века. Это не «массовая культура»; это серьёзная проза, которая определила эпоху.
current_p1_en:
The Great Gatsby, To Kill a Mockingbird, The Catcher in the Rye, The Shining. You love twentieth-century American literature. Not mass culture, but serious prose that defined an era.
Why it works: you're interested in American culture. Through these books you understand the country deeper than through any movie.
Other people sometimes ask: "you read in English?". Sometimes. Translation loses a lot.
What's worth knowing: American classics are often culturally specific. If you don't understand the American South, To Kill a Mockingbird reads at 50% depth. Learn parallel history.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Над пропастью во ржи, Маленький принц, Убить пересмешника, Сто лет одиночества. Тебе нужны книги о росте человека. Не «приключения»; а внутренняя трансформация героя.
current_p1_en:
The Catcher in the Rye, The Little Prince, To Kill a Mockingbird, One Hundred Years of Solitude. You need books about growing up. Not adventures, but inner transformation.
The reason it works: you have your own request for growth. Through books you look for patterns to apply to yourself.
Other people sometimes are surprised: "you read it as self-help?". Not as self-help. As a mirror.
What's worth knowing: coming-of-age books work best at "the right age". Catcher in the Rye at 16 is a different book than at 36. Learn to come back to them. Re-reading gives a different depth.

items_in_category: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
current_p1_ru: Дюна, 451 градус, 1984, Сияние. Тебе нравится литература, которая исследует возможные миры. Не «фэнтези»; а науку и технологию как философскую проблему.
current_p1_en:
Dune, Fahrenheit 451, 1984, The Shining. You like literature that explores possible worlds. Not "fantasy"; science and technology as a philosophical problem.
It works because you have intellectual sensitivity. You need a book to ask questions, not just tell a story.
Other people sometimes don't get it: "sci-fi is for geeks". Maybe. But many of the best 20th-century books are sci-fi. And they're about the present more than many realistic novels.
What's worth knowing: sci-fi requires patience. Dune is 800 pages of complex terminology. Learn to accept it. And don't give up after the first 100 pages — the best parts often come after the introduction.

current_p1_ru: Ты слушал Касту, Басту до его попсы, Смоки Мо, Легалайза. Это был ранний российский рэп — без бюджетов, без гламура, с настоящим словом и улицей. Ты помнишь, как это было до того, как всё стало индустрией.
current_p1_en:
You listened to Kasta, Basta before he went pop, Smoki Mo, Legalize. It was early Russian rap: no budgets, no glamour, just the word and the street. You remember how it sounded before everything became an industry.
The reason it works: you value originality. You understand this era in Russian rap was the only one when nobody was looking back at the West yet — everyone was making their own school, their own vocabulary, their own vibe. And since then there hasn't been that level of independence.
People sometimes don't remember these names: "Smoki Mo? Who's that?". You nod sadly. That's the problem — real founders are forgotten quickly, and today's scene is built on their shoulders, not realizing.
What's worth knowing: preserving memory of roots is honorable, but sometimes becomes a refusal of the present. If you say "everything after 2010 isn't rap" — you're a captive of nostalgia. Today's guys also do strong work, just in another language. Learn to hear across eras. Roots + trunk + branches — that's one tree.

current_p1_ru: Ты слышал Касту и Басту из Ростова, Смоки Мо и Легалайза из Москвы, Тимати когда он только начинал. Это была сцена, которая физически жила между двумя городами, и ты был частью этой географии — даже если жил в третьем месте.
current_p1_en:
You heard Kasta and Basta from Rostov, Smoki Mo and Legalize from Moscow, Timati when he was just starting. It was a scene physically stretched between cities, and you were part of that geography — even if you lived somewhere else.
It works because you understand: places give birth to sound. Not every rap can be made in any city. The Rostov ones had their own intonation, the Moscow ones — another, and you heard this difference.
People sometimes don't think about geography. You don't care. You have a map in your head showing where each school was born.
What's worth knowing: geo-attachment is a great analytical tool, but the world globalizes. Now a rapper in Yakutsk can sound like Atlanta, and vice versa. Learn to track these sound migrations. Geo isn't the predictor it once was.

current_p1_ru: Канье, Lil Wayne, Eminem, Snoop. Эти ребята в 2007 были на пике массовой популярности. Тебе нравилось, что рэп вышел из андеграунда и стал главной музыкой эпохи. Ты не стыдился любить мейнстрим — потому что мейнстрим тогда был хорошим.
current_p1_en:
Kanye, Lil Wayne, Eminem, Snoop. These guys in 2007 were at the peak of mass popularity. You liked that rap had come out of the underground and become the main music of the era. You weren't ashamed to love mainstream — because mainstream then was good.
Why this lands: 2007 was an unusual year — mass rap didn't drop in quality, it grew. Loving the top charts wasn't "cheap"; in the charts stood albums today considered classics.
People sometimes confuse you with a modern mainstream fan: "you listened to mass stuff". You don't argue. Only the mass of that time was on a different level than the mass of now.
What's worth knowing: "the golden mainstream era" is a rare phenomenon. Now the mass is often weak, and loving it is something else. Learn to hear today's mainstream tracks honestly: something weaker, something at the level of 2007. Sometimes pearls exist now too. Don't reject outright.

current_p1_ru: 1984, О дивный новый мир, 451 градус, Мы. Тебе ближе антиутопии о государстве, контролирующем мысль и поведение. Большой Брат, Министерство Правды, нумера вместо имён.
current_p1_en:
1984, Brave New World, Fahrenheit 451, We. The dystopias closest to you are about the state controlling thought and behavior. Big Brother, the Ministry of Truth, numbers instead of names.
This works because you have sensitivity to freedom. These books aren't fiction — they're warnings, and you hear them.
Other people sometimes say: "you're paranoid". Not paranoid — informed. Different things.
What's worth knowing: 20th-century totalitarian dystopias often feel "not about us". But many of their warnings are now more relevant than they seemed. Learn to see parallels. Not for panic — for understanding.

current_p1_ru: О дивный новый мир, Этот идеальный день, Машина останавливается, Не отпускай меня. Тебе ближе антиутопии не о репрессиях, а о слишком комфортной системе. Где счастье — это и есть инструмент порабощения.
current_p1_en:
Brave New World, This Perfect Day, The Machine Stops, Never Let Me Go. The dystopias closest to you aren't about open repression, but about a system that's too comfortable. Happiness itself becomes the instrument of control.
Why it works: you have a mature view of control. Many people think a bad system looks cruel; you understand the worst one may look perfectly comfortable and leave you no choice.
Other people sometimes don't get it: "but in Brave New World everyone is happy". Everyone. And that's the whole horror.
What's worth knowing: these dystopias are more relevant than the totalitarian ones. Huxley in 1932 described modern society more accurately than Orwell. Learn to see this — current threats are usually "comfortable", not "jackbooted".

current_p1_ru: Рассказ служанки, Притча о сеятеле, Не отпускай меня, Повелитель мух. Тебе важна гендерная и социальная справедливость в антиутопии. Эти книги — о том, как общество превращает людей в средства.
current_p1_en:
The Handmaid's Tale, Parable of the Sower, Never Let Me Go, Lord of the Flies. Gender and social justice in dystopia matter to you. These books are about how society turns people into tools.
The reason it works: you have a critical view of hierarchy. Dystopia for you isn't "about the state" but about how any system can dehumanize.
Other people sometimes accuse: "you're at it again with feminism". Not about feminism — about morality.
What's worth knowing: these dystopias often get adapted to screen. The Handmaid's Tale series is a different work than the book. Learn to tell them apart. And remember: the book author is usually deeper than the showrunner.

current_p1_ru: Заводной апельсин, Голодные игры, Повелитель мух, Дорога. Тебя цепляют антиутопии о телесном насилии. Не «контроль мысли»; а реальная физическая жестокость как системная.
current_p1_en:
A Clockwork Orange, The Hunger Games, Lord of the Flies, The Road. What grabs you are dystopias of bodily violence. Not thought control, but physical cruelty turned into a system.
It works because you have the willingness to look at the truth. Many readers can't take such books; you can.
Other people sometimes can't take it: "A Clockwork Orange is just…". It's literature. Brutal, but necessary.
What's worth knowing: these books are hard to read in a row. Three "hard" dystopias in a month and you carry it emotionally. Learn to alternate.
